1:3.headline: Return to me and I will return: Malbim says you go first
1:3.body: Malbim says no more prophets will be sent to warn them, so the people must start the return themselves, and God will answer. Metzudat David says God's answer is to rest his presence among them.

sources.quote: שמעתה לא ישלח עוד נביאים מזהירים להשיבם אליו, (כי אחרי הנביאים האחרונים נפסקה הנבואה) ומעתה צריכים הם להשתדל מעצמם לשוב בתשובה שעז"א שובו אלי ועי"כ אשוב אליכם, שאתם תהיו המתחילים והמתעוררים בעצמכם לשוב
sources.says: Malbim says no more warning prophets will be sent, so they must work to return by themselves: "return to me, and I will return to you", with the people the ones who start.

sources.quote: שכשם שתתעורר לשוב אל ה' לעמת זה ישוב ה' אליך
sources.says: Malbim says that as you rouse yourself to return to God, so God returns to you, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: שובו אלי ואז אשוב אליכם להשרות שכינתי בתוככם
sources.says: Metzudat David says: return to me, and then I will return to you, to rest my presence among you.

1:5.headline: "Do the prophets live forever?": a plain question, or no more prophets?
1:5.body: Rashi reads it as a plain question: the prophets did not live forever, but what they said came true. Malbim and Ibn Ezra, citing Yefet, read it as a sign that no new prophets will come. Radak records a saying of the sages in which the people use the question as a comeback.

sources.quote: וְכִי הַנְּבִיאִים הָיָה לָהֶם לְעוֹלָם לִחְיוֹת? אַךְ סוֹפָן מוֹכִיחַ כִּי אֱמֶת הָיָה דִּבְרֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the prophets did not have to live forever, but the outcome proves their words were true.

sources.quote: והנביאים ששלחתי אז הלעולם יחיו, כי נביאים חדשים לא אשלח עוד
sources.says: Malbim says: will the prophets I sent then live forever? I will not send new prophets.

sources.quote: ויפת אמר: כי הטעם דעו כי תפסק הנבואה וזה טעם הלעולם יחיו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Yefet took it to mean: know that prophecy will stop.

sources.quote: אמרו לו והנביאים שלא חטאו איה הם היכן הם וחזרו והודו לו
sources.says: Radak records a saying that the people replied: and the prophets who did not sin, where are they? Then they returned and admitted it.

1:8.headline: "I saw in the night": a night vision, or the night of exile?
1:8.body: Radak says plainly that Zechariah saw this in a night vision. A saying of the sages in Radak says God wished to turn the whole world to night. Malbim says trouble is compared to night, so each of the four kingdoms is its own night.

sources.quote: ואמר ראיתי הלילה במראות הלילה ראיתי זאת המראה שראיתי
sources.says: Radak says "I saw the night" means I saw this vision in night visions.

sources.quote: ראיתי הלילה בקש הקב"ה להפך את כל העולם כולו ללילה
sources.says: Radak records the sages' reading: "I saw the night" means the Holy One wanted to turn the whole world into night.

sources.quote: כי הצרה נמשלה ללילה
sources.says: Malbim says trouble is compared to night.

1:8.headline: The "man" on the horse: an angel, or God himself?
1:8.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra say the man is an angel, like "the man Gabriel". A saying of the sages in Radak says the only "man" is the Holy One, citing "the Lord is a man of war".

sources.quote: וְהִנֵּה אִישׁ. מַלְאָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the man is an angel.

sources.quote: והנה איש - מלאך, כמו: והאיש גבריאל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the man is an angel, like "the man Gabriel".

sources.quote: והנה איש רוכב ואין איש אלא הקב"ה שנאמר ה' איש מלחמה
sources.says: Radak records the sages' reading: the man riding is the Holy One, as it is said "the Lord is a man of war".

1:8.headline: שרקים: Rashi says he does not know what colour this is
1:8.body: Rashi admits he does not know the colour and gives the Targum's word. Metzudat Zion says it means streaked in mixed colours. Malbim says it is a mix of red and white, and Ibn Ezra ties it to the word שורק.

sources.quote: לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מַה צֶבַע הוּא, וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know what colour it is, and that Jonathan translated it.

sources.quote: שרוקים. מצויירים בצבעים מחולפים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means drawn in mixed colours.

sources.quote: והשרוקים הם מורכבים מאדום ולבן והוא ממוצע ביניהם
sources.says: Malbim says the שרוקים are made of red and white and are in between them.

sources.quote: ומלת שרוקים מגזרת שורקה במראה שורק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from שורקה, in the look of a שורק.

1:8.headline: The myrtles are the righteous, and give Esther her name Hadassah
1:8.body: Metzudat Zion says הדס is a sweet-smelling tree. Radak says Israel is likened to myrtles for the good smell of its mitzvot, and a saying of the sages says the myrtles are the righteous. Ralbag says Esther's name Hadassah comes from the same picture.

sources.quote: ההדסים. שם אילן המריח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הדסים is the name of a fragrant tree.

sources.quote: לעצי הדס לפי שיש להם ריח טוב כן ישראל שבבבל יש להם ריח מצות
sources.says: Radak says Israel is likened to myrtle trees because they smell good, as Israel in Babylon has the smell of mitzvot.

sources.quote: ואין הדסים אלא צדיקים וכן הוא אומר ויהי אומן את הדסה
sources.says: Radak records the sages' reading: הדסים are only the righteous, as it says "and he brought up Hadassah".

sources.quote: והנה כי כמו שהמשיל הצדיקים להדסים כאמור בין ההדסים אשר במצולה (זכריה א, ח) כן המשיל אותה להדסה
sources.says: Ralbag says that as the righteous are compared to myrtles in Zechariah 1:8, so Esther is compared to Hadassah.

1:8.headline: במצולה: Babylon, a deep place of water, or a pool?
1:8.body: Rashi and Radak say it is Babylon. Metzudat Zion says it is a place of many waters, as in Jonah 2:4. Ibn Ezra says the meaning is hard, and reports two readings: a place name, or a pool with myrtles around it.

sources.quote: בֵּין אִילָנֵי דְהַדַסַּיָּא דִּבְבָבֶל
sources.says: Rashi says it means among the myrtle trees in Babylon.

sources.quote: במצולה. היא בבל
sources.says: Radak says במצולה is Babylon.

sources.quote: מקום רבוי המים עניינו כמו ותשליכני מצולה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a place of much water, like "you threw me into the deep".

sources.quote: ופירוש במצולה קשה. ויפת אמר: כי הוא שם מקום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning of במצולה is hard, and that Yefet said it is a place name.

sources.quote: ורבי משה הכהן אמר: כי במצולה בריכת מים וסביבותיה הדסים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Rabbi Moshe the Priest said במצולה is a pool of water with myrtles around it.

1:9.headline: "I will show you": see with the eyes, or tell you?
1:9.body: Radak says it would be more natural to say "I will let you hear", since only the horses were shown. So "show" may stand for "tell", because sight stands for the other senses, as in "all the people saw the sounds". Malbim reads it plainly: in the later visions I will show you what these mean.

sources.quote: אפשר כי אראך כמו אשמיעך כי חוש הראות נשאל לשאר החושים לפי שהוא החזק שבכלם כמו שאמר וכל העם רואים את הקולות
sources.says: Radak says אראך may be like "I will let you hear", since sight is borrowed for the other senses as the strongest of them, as in "all the people saw the sounds".

sources.quote: ויאמר אלי אני אראך מה המה אלה, ר"ל שבמראות האחרות אשר אראך תבין פירוש הדברים האלה ועניניהם
sources.says: Malbim says it means that in the other visions I will show you, you will understand the meaning of these.

1:10.headline: The horses "walk the earth": to look, or to take land?
1:10.body: Rashi says they go to see how calm the star-worshipping nations are. Metzudat David says they go to take land that is not theirs. Ibn Ezra and Radak compare them to the Accuser in Job, who goes to and fro on the earth.

sources.quote: לִרְאוֹת אֶת שַׁלְוַת הָעַוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they go to see the ease of the star-worshippers.

sources.quote: להתהלך בארץ לארכה ולרחבה לרשת משכנות לא להם כל אחד בזמנו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they walk the earth, its length and breadth, to take dwellings not theirs, each in his time.

sources.quote: אלה הסוסים שלוחי השם לשוט בארץ, כמו שטן איוב שגם הוא מלאך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these horses are God's messengers to roam the earth, like the Accuser in Job, who is also an angel.

sources.quote: על דרך שאמר השטן משוט בארץ ומתהלך בה
sources.says: Radak says this is like what the Accuser said: from roaming the earth and walking on it.

1:11.headline: "Sitting and quiet" is the complaint, not good news
1:11.body: That the whole earth is at rest sounds good, but Radak says it is the grievance: the nations are at ease while Israel suffers. Ibn Ezra says as long as the nations are quiet, Jerusalem is not pitied.

sources.quote: ראינו שלות העכו"ם וישראל בצער לפיכך ענה המלאך ואמר עד מתי אתה לא תרחם את ירושלם
sources.says: Radak says: we saw the ease of the nations while Israel was in pain, so the angel answered: how long will you not pity Jerusalem?

sources.quote: כי כל זמן שיש לגוים השקט לא תרוחם ירושלם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says as long as the nations have quiet, Jerusalem is not pitied.

sources.quote: וכל הארץ יושבת ושוקטת כי פסקו המלחמות, באשר הכל תחת רשותם
sources.says: Malbim says the whole earth is quiet because the wars stopped, since everything is under their rule.

1:12.headline: "How long will you not pity": the stress is on "you"
1:12.body: Malbim says the angel's word אתה is exact: why is it not You, rather than the kingdoms that walk the earth, who pities Jerusalem? Metzudat David says: You are lord over every host above and below, and lord of Israel.

sources.quote: דייק במלת אתה
sources.says: Malbim says he is exact with the word אתה, "you".

sources.quote: הלא אתה שר ישראל ואתה מושל בכל
sources.says: Metzudat David says: are you not the prince of Israel, and you rule over all?

1:14.headline: "I am jealous for Jerusalem": zeal for her, or anger at her enemies?
1:14.body: Ibn Ezra says קנאה joined with ל means zeal for someone's good, and joined with ב it is the opposite. Metzudat Zion and Metzudat David read it here as anger. Rashi quotes the Targum: I will take vengeance for Jerusalem on those who press her.

sources.quote: כל קנאה קשורה עם למ"ד איננה כמו קשורה בבי"ת, והנה זה כמו: המקנא אתה לי והטעם בעבור, כמו: ויקנא השם לארצו - בעבור ארצו והיא קנאה לטוב לאותו הנזכר וכשהיא קשרה בבי"ת, כמו ויקנאו בו פלשתים - היא להפך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says קנאה with ל is jealousy for the good of the one named, while with ב, as in "the Philistines were jealous of him", it is the opposite.

sources.quote: קנאתי. ענין כעס כמו הם קנאוני בלא אל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says קנאתי means anger, like "they made me jealous with what is not God".

sources.quote: בעבור מה שעשו העכו״ם לירושלים ולציון כועס אני הרבה
sources.says: Metzudat David says: because of what the nations did to Jerusalem and Zion, I am very angry.

sources.quote: מִתְפָּרַע אֲנָא פּוּרְעָנוּת דִּין יְרוּשָׁלַיִם מִן הַמְּצִיקִים לָהּ
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: I am taking vengeance for Jerusalem from those who press her.

1:17.headline: "My cities will scatter": into exile, or overflow with good?
1:17.body: Metzudat David reads תפוצנה as scattering: more ruin and exile are still to come. Ibn Ezra and Radak read it as spreading out because of the abundance of good, so the land fills with settlers. Targum Jonathan says the cities will be filled with good.

sources.quote: עוד יבוא חרבן וגלות על הבית השני ויפוצו יושבי ערי יהודה מכל טוב
sources.says: Metzudat David says ruin and exile will still come on the Second Temple, and the people of Judah's cities will be scattered from all good.

sources.quote: עוד תפוצינה - בכל צד מרוב הטובה יגדל היישוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says on every side, from the abundance of good, the settlement will grow.

sources.quote: מרוב טובה ושלוה שיהיה להם תפוצנה הנה והנה כלומר שירבה היישוב
sources.says: Radak says from the abundance of good and peace they will spread here and there, meaning the settlement will grow.

sources.quote: עוֹד יִתְמַלְיָן קִרְוֵי עַמִי טוּבָא
sources.says: Targum Jonathan says the towns of my people will again be filled with good.

11:7.headline: 'Therefore' here may really mean 'truly'
11:7.body: לכן usually means 'therefore'. Rashi and Radak read it as 'truly': the flock really was poor when God began to shepherd it.

sources.quote: אֱמֶת עֲנִיֵּי הַצֹּאן הָיוּ כְּשֶׁהִתְחַלְתִּי לִרְעוֹתָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means that truly the flock was poor when God began to shepherd it.

sources.quote: באמת עניי הצאן מצאתים כשלקחתיה לרעות תחלה
sources.says: Radak says that in truth he found the flock poor when he first took it to shepherd.

11:8.headline: Maimonides hears the staff 'chovlim' scrambled inside 'bachalah'
11:8.body: בחלה, 'loathed', stands alone in the Bible, and Maimonides says the prophet shuffled the letters of חבל into בחל to echo the staff named חובלים. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion note that the word has nothing like it elsewhere.

sources.quote: הרי שהחליף את סדר האותיות של חבל והפכו לבחל
sources.says: Maimonides says the prophet swapped the order of the letters of חבל to make בחל.

sources.quote: ומלת בחלה בי – אין לה חבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word בחלה has no companion word.

sources.quote: ענין מיאוס ותעוב ואין לו דומה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means disgust and loathing and has nothing like it.

11:9.headline: 'A woman' here means 'one': each sheep eats the next
11:9.body: אשה normally means 'woman', but Metzudat Zion says it means 'one', as in 'one to her sister' in Exodus. So each sheep eats the flesh of her companion.

sources.quote: אשה. ר״ל אחת וכן אשה אל אחותה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אשה means 'one', like 'one to her sister'.

sources.quote: תאכלנה אחת בשר חברתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says each one will eat the flesh of her fellow.

11:13.headline: 'I was precious to them' may mean 'I took my honor away'
11:13.body: יקרתי usually means 'valued', but Rashi says here it means removing honor, and the מ of מעליהם shows it. Metzudat David instead reads it as honor placed over their heads like a crown.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן יָקַרְתִּי הוּא הֲסָרַת כָּבוֹד, וְהַמֵּ״ם שֶׁל מֵעֲלֵיהֶם יוֹכִיחַ
sources.says: Rashi says יקרתי is a word of taking honor away, and the מ in מעליהם proves it.

sources.quote: אשר הכבדתי להיות ממעל להם עטרה על ראשם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the honor God placed over them as a crown on their heads.

11:15.headline: 'Foolish' ends in a yod that is not 'my'
11:15.body: אוילי means foolish, a shepherd with no sense. The ending yod looks like 'my', but Radak says it is an ending that marks the quality, as in אכזרי, 'cruel'.

sources.quote: היו"ד ליחס כיו"ד אכזרי
sources.says: Radak says the yod marks the quality, like the yod in אכזרי.

sources.quote: אוילי. שוטה מבלי דעת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אוילי means a fool without knowledge.

11:16.headline: 'The young one' may be a wandering sheep, or a tender lamb
11:16.body: נער usually means a boy, but Rashi says here it means the silly sheep that do not know how to come back to the fold. Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say it is the tender lamb.

sources.quote: הַנַּעַר – הַשּׁוֹטוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן יוֹדְעוֹת לָבוֹא אֶל הַדִּיר
sources.says: Rashi says הנער means the silly sheep that do not know how to come to the fold.

sources.quote: הנער. ר״ל הטלה הרך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says הנער means the tender lamb.

sources.quote: הנער - שה אובד הקטן לא יבקש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הנער is the small lost lamb that he will not seek.

11:17.headline: 'Of the idol' may mean 'worthless'
11:17.body: אליל usually means an idol, but Metzudat Zion and Radak say it can mean something of no use, as in Job. So the 'shepherd of the idol' is a worthless shepherd.

sources.quote: האליל. ענין דבר שאין בו תועלת
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אליל means a thing with no use.

sources.quote: כמו רופאי אליל דבר שאינו מועיל
sources.says: Radak says it is like 'healers of nothing', a thing that does no good.

sources.quote: אוי לך אתה רועה מבלי מועיל
sources.says: Metzudat David glosses the shepherd as one who does no good.

11:17.headline: The 'right eye' means wisdom, or the shepherd's greedy look
11:17.body: Ibn Ezra says the arm is strength and the eye is wisdom and counsel, and Radak says it is the eye of the heart. Rashi reads it as the shepherd's eye picking out the rich to rob.

sources.quote: וטעם זרוע הכח שיסור והעין עין חכמה, והעצה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the arm is strength and the eye is the eye of wisdom and counsel.

sources.quote: ור"ל עין ימינו עין הלב
sources.says: Radak says the right eye means the eye of the heart.

sources.quote: שֶׁנָּתַן עֵין יְמִינוֹ בָּהֶם לָדַעַת מִי הָעֲשִׁירִים לָבֹז
sources.says: Rashi says the shepherd set his right eye on the flock to learn who is rich so he can rob them.

12:3.headline: Lifting the stone tears the lifters' hands
12:3.body: Radak explains the picture: people trying to hoist a huge stone onto their shoulders scrape their hands on it. The Targum reads the words differently, as being plundered.

sources.quote: ובעוד שמרימים אותה מן הארץ להרימה על כתפם יעשו בה שריטות בידיהם
sources.says: Radak says those lifting the stone onto their shoulders get scratches on their hands.

sources.quote: שרוט ישרטו. ענין תלישת הבשר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the words mean tearing of flesh, as in Leviticus 21:5.

sources.quote: כָּל אֶנְסָהָא אִתְבְּזָזָא יִתְבַּזְזוּן
sources.says: The Targum renders it as being plundered.

12:3.headline: Gathered against her, or gathered in death?
12:3.body: ונאספו usually means they will gather, and Malbim reads it as Gog's armies massing to take the city. Metzudat Zion reads it as dying, as in that whole generation was gathered, so the nations will perish beside Jerusalem.

sources.quote: ונאספו. ענין כליון ומיתה כמו כל הדור ההוא נאספו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word here means destruction and death.

sources.quote: ונאספו עליה. אצלה בסמוך
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as the nations coming to an end right beside her.

sources.quote: שחיל גוג ומגוג יתאספו כולם לכבשה
sources.says: Malbim reads it as the armies of Gog and Magog gathering to capture the city.

12:4.headline: Two blows: confusion in the heart, blindness in the eyes
12:4.body: The horses are struck with תמהון, bewilderment, and later with עורון, blindness. Radak says these are two separate blows, one to the heart and one to the eyes.

sources.quote: והתמהון הוא בלב והעורון הוא בעינים
sources.says: Radak says the bewilderment is in the heart and the blindness is in the eyes.

sources.quote: ר״ל יאבדו אבידת הלב כאדם המתמה ומתייאש
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will lose heart like a stunned man who gives up hope.

12:7.headline: Tents of Judah: an army camp, or Judah's towns?
12:7.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra say the verse says tents because an army besieging a city lives in tents, and Judah's men were in that camp. The Targum instead reads it as the towns of the house of Judah.

sources.quote: לפי שהצרים על עיר יושבים באהלים לפיכך אמר אהלי יהודה
sources.says: Radak says it says tents because those besieging a city live in tents.

sources.quote: כי כן דרך המחנות שוכנים באהלים סביב העיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says armies camp in tents around a city.

sources.quote: יַת קִרְוַיָא דְבֵית יְהוּדָה
sources.says: The Targum renders it the towns of the house of Judah.

12:8.headline: The one who stumbles: the weak, or the one who sins?
12:8.body: Rashi and Radak read הנכשל as the weakest person, who will be as strong as David. Malbim reads it as someone who stumbles into sin, who will be like David in repenting at once.

sources.quote: הַנִּכְשָׁל בָּהֶם. הַחַלָּשׁ שֶׁבָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means the weakest among them.

sources.quote: החלש שבהם יהיה כדוד שהיה גבור חיל ואיש מלחמה
sources.says: Radak says the weakest will be like David, a mighty warrior.

sources.quote: וגם אם ימצא בהם איש שיכשל בחטא יהיה כדוד שעשה תשובה תיכף
sources.says: Malbim says even one who stumbles into sin will be like David, who repented at once.

12:8.headline: Like God here means like angels or great princes
12:8.body: אלהים usually means God, but here the house of David becomes כאלהים. Rashi follows the Targum, like great ones, and explains it as angels, which the verse spells out next.

sources.quote: כֵּאלֹהִים. ״כְּרַבְרְבִין״ (תרגום יונתן), כְּמַלְאָכִים
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum's like great ones and explains it as like angels.

sources.quote: כאלהים - מלאכים וככה פירושו כמלאך ה' לפניהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means angels, as the next words like an angel of the LORD explain.

sources.quote: וּבֵית דָוִיד כְּרַבְרְבִין
sources.says: The Targum renders it like great ones.

12:9.headline: God seeks to destroy: searching for guilt, or for merit?
12:9.body: Rashi first reads it as God looking closely into the nations' sins before destroying them. He then brings the Sages' reading: God searches them, and if they have merit, he leaves them alone.

sources.quote: אֲבַקֵּשׁ בְּהַשְׁמָדָתָם וַאֲדַקְדֵּק בַּעֲוֹנָם
sources.says: Rashi says God will look closely into their sins.

sources.quote: אִם יֵשׁ לָהֶם זְכוּת – אֲנִיחֵם, וְאִם לָאו – אַשְׁמִידֵם
sources.says: Rashi brings the Sages: if they have merit God leaves them, and if not he destroys them.

sources.quote: אבקש ואעשה כלומר אשים כל רצוני להשמידם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means God will set his whole will on destroying them.

12:12.headline: Which Nathan: the prophet, or David's son?
12:12.body: Rashi gives both: Nathan the prophet, or Nathan son of David. Ibn Ezra says it need not be Solomon's brother, since the house of David already covers David's sons.

sources.quote: בֵּית נָתָן. הַנָּבִיא. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: נָתָן בֶּן דָּוִד
sources.says: Rashi says it is Nathan the prophet, and some say Nathan son of David.

sources.quote: ולהיות בית נתן אחי שלמה אין צורך, כי בית דוד שם כולל לשניהם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says there is no need to make it Solomon's brother, since house of David already includes both.

14:3.headline: קרב is close combat: God fights hand to hand
14:3.body: Malbim says קרב is fighting at close range, unlike war from a distance with arrows, so God will fight with no natural go-between. Rashi, with the Targum, says this 'day of battle' is the day God fought at the Sea of Reeds.

sources.quote: כי יש הבדל בין קרב ובין מלחמה, שבקרב הוא לוחם עם אויבו בקרוב ומתאבק עמו
sources.says: Malbim says קרב differs from מלחמה: in קרב one fights the enemy up close and wrestles with him.

sources.quote: כְּיוֹם אֲגָחוּתֵיהּ קְרָב עַל יַמָּא דְּסוּף
sources.says: Rashi quotes the Targum: like the day He waged battle at the Sea of Reeds.

14:4.headline: God's feet 'stand': Maimonides reads it as lasting, not standing
14:4.body: עמד can mean to stand up, to stop, or to last. Maimonides says that said of God it always means the last one: the wonders God causes on the Mount of Olives will hold firm.

sources.quote: ויש לו משמעות של קביעות וקיום
sources.says: Maimonides says one meaning of עמד is to be fixed and lasting.

sources.quote: ותהיינה סיבותיו קבועות, כלומר הדברים שהוא גרם להם
sources.says: Maimonides reads this verse as: his causes, the things he brought about, will be fixed.

14:4.headline: God's 'feet' on the mountain are the wonders he causes
14:4.body: Maimonides reads רגל, foot, as 'cause', so God's feet on the Mount of Olives are the wonders he will cause there. Radak follows him, and Metzudat David calls the verse a figure of speech for the mountain splitting.

sources.quote: היא קיום סיבותיו, כלומר הנפלאות שיופיעו אז באותו מקום, שהוא יתעלה הסיבה להן
sources.says: Maimonides says the verse means the lasting of his causes: the wonders that will appear there, of which God is the cause.

sources.quote: כמו ויברך אותך לרגלי בסבתי כן רגליו רוצה לומר קיום סבותיו
sources.says: Radak brings Maimonides: as 'the LORD blessed you לרגלי' means because of me, so 'his feet' means his causes.

sources.quote: הוא ענין משל שבא לומר שיבקע הר הזיתים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a figure of speech meaning the Mount of Olives will split.

14:5.headline: 'You will flee', or 'it will be blocked'?
14:5.body: ונסתם can mean 'you will flee' or 'it will be blocked up'. Rashi, with the Targum, reads the valley filling up; Radak and Malbim also read people fleeing into the new valley, as their fathers fled the earthquake.

sources.quote: וּכְשֶׁיִּמָּשֵׁךְ חֲצִי הַר הַזֵּיתִים אֵצֶל הַר שֶׁבִּצְפוֹנוֹ, יִסָּתֵם הַגַּיְא שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says that when half the Mount of Olives moves next to the northern hill, the valley between them will be blocked.

sources.quote: ויונתן תרגם ונסתם תחלת הפסוק ויסתתים דומה שהיה קורא ונסתם בשקל כי נכתם עונך
sources.says: Radak notes that the Targum read the first ונסתם as 'will be blocked', with a different vowel.

sources.quote: שכולם ינוסו אל הגיא שבין שני ההרים שיתפרדו עתה
sources.says: Malbim gives the other reading: everyone will flee into the valley between the two halves of the mountain.

14:5.headline: Azal: a place name, or 'the heights'?
14:5.body: Ibn Ezra reads אצל as the name of a place the valley will reach. Rashi reads it as height: the valley will fill up to the mountaintops. Radak gives both readings.

sources.quote: ונסתם, אל אצל - שם מקום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אצל is the name of a place.

sources.quote: אֶל גֹּבַהּ רָאשֵׁי הֶהָרִים שֶׁמִּכָּאן וּמִכָּאן
sources.says: Rashi says it means up to the height of the mountaintops on either side.

sources.quote: ואצל ענינו גבוה כמו ואל אצילי בני ישראל שענינו גדולי ישראל
sources.says: Radak says אצל can mean high, as in 'the nobles of Israel', after also calling it a place name.

14:5.headline: 'The LORD will come': his promises will come true
14:5.body: בא means to come or to enter. Maimonides says that said of God it can mean his word coming true: 'the LORD will come with all the holy ones' means his promises through the prophets will be kept. Radak brings this reading.

sources.quote: חלות דברו, כלומר קיום הבטחותיו שהבטיח ביד נביאיו
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse means the arrival of God's word: the keeping of the promises he made through his prophets.

sources.quote: ובא ה' אלהים על ידי כל הקדושים עמך המדברים לישראל
sources.says: Radak brings Maimonides' reading: God will come through all the holy ones who spoke to Israel.

14:6.headline: A rare word for light that has thickened, like ice
14:6.body: קפאון comes from the verb for freezing or curdling. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as thick, dark light, like water turned to ice. Malbim takes it as the moon's light, which is only borrowed from the sun.

sources.quote: קָפוּי וְחָשׁוּךְ וְעָב כַּקֶּרַח שֶׁנִּקְפָּה וּמַגְלִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it means congealed, dark and thick, like ice that freezes over, and compares Job's 'curdled me like cheese'.

sources.quote: ר״ל חשך כדבר הנקפה והוא דבר צלול הנהפך להיות עב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means darkness, like something clear that has thickened.

sources.quote: ולא אור הירח וככבים שהם רק מקבלים האור
sources.says: Malbim reads it as the light of the moon and stars, which only receive their light.

14:9.headline: 'His name one': one name for God himself, not many titles
14:9.body: Rashi reads it simply: every mouth will speak his name. Ibn Ezra says the four-letter name will be read as written. Maimonides says people will stop thinking God's many titles name many qualities, and will call him by the one name that points to him alone.

sources.quote: שֶׁיְּהֵא שְׁמוֹ נִזְכָּר בְּפִי כֻּלָּם
sources.says: Rashi says his name will be spoken by everyone.

sources.quote: ושמו אחד - הוא השם הנכבד הנודע על יד משה עבדו, ויקרא בפי כל ככתבו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the honored name made known through Moses, which everyone will pronounce as it is written.

sources.quote: כלומר שכפי שהוא אחד כך הוא ייקרא אז בשם אחד בלבד, והוא המורה על העצמות לבדה, ואינו נגזר
sources.says: Maimonides says that as God is one, he will then be called by one name only, a name that points to his essence and is not built from his actions.

14:10.headline: Jerusalem will 'sit': it will stand firm and unchanging
14:10.body: ישב means to sit. Maimonides says that because a seated person is at his most settled, the word also means fixed and unchanging, so the verse promises that Jerusalem will last at its height. Rashi reads it plainly: in its own place.

sources.quote: נאמר בהבטחה לירושלם שתתמיד ותהיה יציבה בהיותה בדרגה העליונה ביותר
sources.says: Maimonides says this verse promises Jerusalem that it will endure and stay firm at its highest level.

sources.quote: הושאל המונח לכל מצב יציב וקבוע שאינו משתנה
sources.says: Maimonides says the word for sitting was borrowed for any fixed state that does not change.

sources.quote: וְיָשְׁבָה תַּחְתֶּיהָ. בִּמְקוֹמָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means it will sit in its own place.

14:10.headline: The king's wine pits, or the ocean God dug?
14:10.body: יקבי המלך are the king's wine pits, where wine flows down from the press. Rashi also brings a midrash: the King is God and his pits are the ocean, so Jerusalem will reach the ends of the world.

sources.quote: בורות שלפני הגת והיין יורד בהן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are pits in front of the winepress that the wine runs down into.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: יִקְבֵי מֶלֶךְ יָם אוֹקְיָנוֹס, שֶׁתַּגִּיעַ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם עַד סוֹף כָּל הָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi brings a midrash that the king's pits are the ocean, so Jerusalem will reach the end of the world, pits dug by the King of kings.

14:13.headline: His hand rises against his friend, or falls off?
14:13.body: ועלתה usually means 'it went up', and Rashi reads it so: in the panic, the stronger man wins. Ibn Ezra and Radak say it can also mean 'cut off': a man's hand will come away as he grabs his friend's, like the melting flesh of the plague.

sources.quote: כָּל דְּאַלִּים גָּבַר
sources.says: Rashi says whoever is stronger prevails.

sources.quote: ועלתה - כמשמעו, או כמו ונכרתה וככה יצועי עלה הכרת ופסק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is either the plain sense, 'went up', or 'was cut off'.

sources.quote: תפסק ידו כשיחזיק ביד רעהו כמו שאמר המק בשרו
sources.says: Radak says his hand will be severed when he grabs his friend's hand, like the melting flesh described before.

14:16.headline: Bowing to the King, the LORD, or to the LORD's king?
14:16.body: Radak reads למלך ה' צבאות as 'to the King, the LORD of hosts': the nations now know God rules the earth. Ibn Ezra points to the vowel under the ל and reads 'to the king of the LORD', meaning the Messiah.

sources.quote: שהם הכירוהו למלך על כל הארץ
sources.says: Radak says they recognized God as king over all the earth.

sources.quote: נראה כי הוא סמוך השם הוא המשיח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the vowel shows the word is joined to God's name, so it means the king of the LORD, the Messiah.

14:17.headline: Why the punishment for skipping Sukkot is no rain
14:17.body: Rashi stops on rain to explain the fit. The festival's rites, the four species and the water offering, are prayers for rain, since Sukkot is when the year's rain is decided. So nations that scorn Sukkot get no rain.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁמִּצְוֹת הֶחָג עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים הֵם
sources.says: Rashi says the festival's commandments are about rain: the four species and the water libation, to win favor for the rains.

sources.quote: שבחג נדונים על המים ומנסכים נסוך המים
sources.says: Malbim says that on the festival the world is judged for water and the water libation is poured.

14:18.headline: Egypt needs no rain, so what does 'not on them' mean?
14:18.body: Egypt is watered by the Nile, not rain. Rashi, with the Targum, reads 'not on them' as: the Nile will not rise for them. Ibn Ezra and Radak read on: the plague will fall on them instead.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר: לֹא יַשְׁקֶה אוֹתָם נִילוּס
sources.says: Rashi says it means the Nile will not water them.

sources.quote: ומלת עליהם תשרת בעבור אחרת, עליהם תהיה המגפה המק בשרו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word עליהם does double duty: on them will be the plague of melting flesh.

sources.quote: והם לא ירד עליהם מטר כל השנים ולא יצטרכו למטר אם כן מה יהיה עונשם
sources.says: Radak asks what Egypt's punishment can be, since rain never falls there and they do not need it, and answers that it is the plague.

14:20.headline: Horse bells, or the shadow a running horse casts?
14:20.body: מצלות appears only here. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say they are bells hung on horses, from צלצל, to ring. Radak brings a reading of the sages from צל, shadow: the land will grow as far as a horse can run by noon, when its shadow falls under it.

sources.quote: עַל הַנְּקִישׁוֹת שֶׁתּוֹלִין לַסּוּס לְנוֹי בֵּין עֵינָיו
sources.says: Rashi says they are the clappers hung between a horse's eyes for decoration.

sources.quote: על כי מקשקשים ומשמיעים קול והוא מל׳ בצלצלי שמע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are bells, named for the sound they make, from 'clanging cymbals'.

sources.quote: עתיד הקדוש ברוך הוא להוסיף על ארץ ישראל עד שעה שהסוס רץ ומצל
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: God will enlarge the land of Israel as far as a horse runs until it casts a shadow.

14:21.headline: No more 'Canaanite': a trader, a Gibeonite, or 'no poor here'
14:21.body: כנעני can mean a merchant, and Rashi and Ibn Ezra read it so: no one will need to trade in God's house. Rashi also hears כאן עני, 'a poor man here': there will be none. Metzudat David reads the Gibeonites, Canaanites who once served the Temple.

sources.quote: לֹא יִצְטָרְכוּ לִסְחוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says they will not need to trade, as in Isaiah's 'her כנענים, the honored of the earth'.

sources.quote: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אֵין כָּאן עָנִי
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: there is no poor man here.

sources.quote: כנעני סוחר, וטעם שלא ימכר אחד מן הסירות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says כנעני is a merchant: not one of the pots will be sold.

sources.quote: לפי שמאז היו הגבעונים מבני כנען חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים לבית ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says the Gibeonites, of Canaanite descent, used to cut wood and draw water for the Temple, and will no longer.

3:1.headline: The accuser: an angel, a human enemy, or the evil urge
3:1.body: השטן means the opposer, from the same verb as לשטנו, 'to oppose him', at the end of the verse. Metzudat Zion calls him an accusing angel, while Ibn Ezra and Radak see the enemies, like Sanballat, who fought the rebuilding.

sources.quote: השטן. מלאך מקטרג
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the satan is an accusing angel.

sources.quote: לשטנו. ענין קטרוג וכן כתבו שטנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says לשטנו means to accuse, as in 'they wrote an accusation' in Ezra.

sources.quote: והשטן - אויב כמו שעשה סנבלט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the satan is an enemy, like Sanballat.

sources.quote: השטן משל לסנבלט וחבריו שהיו שוטנים אותם
sources.says: Radak says the satan is a figure for Sanballat and his allies, who opposed the builders.

sources.quote: הוא שטן, הוא יצר רע, הוא מלאך המות
sources.says: Maimonides cites the sages: the satan, the evil urge and the angel of death are one thing, and he applies it to this verse.

3:2.headline: A stick pulled from the fire: real flames, or exile?
3:2.body: An אוד is a stick used to stir a fire. Rashi cites a tradition that Joshua was really thrown into a fire and came out alive, while Radak reads the fire as the exile he escaped.

sources.quote: אוד. הוא העץ שמנדנדים בו האש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says an אוד is the stick used to stir the fire.

sources.quote: שֶׁהֻשְׁלַךְ עִם אַחְאָב בֶּן קוֹלָיָה וַחֲבֵרוֹ לָאוּר
sources.says: Rashi cites the Talmud: Joshua was thrown into the fire together with Ahab son of Kolaiah and his companion.

sources.quote: וכן זה מוצל מאש הגלות לבא לירושלם
sources.says: Radak says Joshua was saved from the fire of exile to come to Jerusalem, and adds that the sages read it literally.

3:4.headline: 'Your sin' here may mean your punishment and shame
3:4.body: עון usually means a sin. Ibn Ezra says here it means the punishment, pain and disgrace Joshua carried, as he also reads גדול עוני מנשוא.

sources.quote: ומלת עונך כדרך גדול עוני מנשוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עונך is used as in גדול עוני מנשוא, which he reads as 'my punishment and pain are too great'.

sources.quote: העברתי מעליך - עונשך וצערך וחרפתך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God removed Joshua's punishment, pain and disgrace.

sources.quote: עונך. פי' כי הבגדים הצואים הם משל לעון
sources.says: Radak says the word shows that the filthy clothes are a figure for sin.

3:6.headline: The angel 'witnessed' to Joshua, meaning he warned him
3:6.body: ויעד comes from עד, a witness. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it means a warning here, because a warning is usually given before witnesses so no one can deny it later.

sources.quote: וַיָּעַד. לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה, כְּמוֹ וְאָעִידָה בָם אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says ויעד means a warning, as in 'I will call heaven to witness against them'.

sources.quote: ענין התראה כי רוב המתרים מתרים בעדים למען לא יכחש לאחר זמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means warning, because most warnings are given before witnesses so the warned one cannot deny it later.

3:7.headline: Angels are called 'the ones who stand'
3:7.body: The commentators stop on why angels are called העמדים. Rashi says angels never sit and have no joints to bend, and Radak says they stand and last forever.

sources.quote: שְׂרָפִים וּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם יְשִׁיבָה
sources.says: Rashi says the standing ones are seraphim and ministering angels, who do not sit.

sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם קְפָצִים
sources.says: Rashi says angels are called standing ones, citing this verse, because they have no joints.

sources.quote: הם המלאכים שהם עומדים וקיימים לעולם
sources.says: Radak says they are the angels, who stand and endure forever.

3:7.headline: Walking among angels: after death, or through his children?
3:7.body: The Aramaic translation, cited by Rashi, says God will revive Joshua and let him walk among the angels, and Radak says it hints at his soul after death. By the plain sense, Rashi says, it promises that his sons will be worthy.

sources.quote: וּבַאֲחָיוּת מֵיתַיָּא אֲחַיֵּינָךְ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Aramaic: when the dead are revived, I will revive you.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ: מְבַשְּׂרוֹ עַל בָּנָיו שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ לֶעָתִיד
sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is a promise that his sons will be worthy in the future.

sources.quote: תלך ביניהם וזה רמז לנשמתו בהפרדו מהגוף
sources.says: Radak says walking among the angels hints at his soul once it leaves the body.

3:8.headline: The 'Sprout': Zerubbabel's slow rise, or the Messiah
3:8.body: צמח means a sprout. Rashi and Radak say it is Zerubbabel, whose greatness grew little by little like a plant, while the Aramaic translation and Malbim say it is the Messiah, growing from David's line like a hidden seed.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֵׁם שֶׁצָּמְחָה גְּדֻלָּתוֹ מְעַט מְעַט
sources.says: Rashi says Zerubbabel is called צמח because his greatness sprouted little by little.

sources.quote: ותצמח גדולתו כצמח האדמה שהולך וגדל
sources.says: Radak says Zerubbabel's greatness will grow like a plant from the ground.

sources.quote: יַת עַבְדִי מְשִׁיחָא
sources.says: The Aramaic translation reads 'my servant the Messiah'.

sources.quote: וקראו בשם צמח לרמז כי עתה נכרת חוטר מגזע ישי והוא נעלם טמון בארץ
sources.says: Malbim says the Messiah is called צמח because David's line is now cut down and hidden in the ground like a seed.

3:9.headline: Seven eyes on one stone: carved eyes, or God's watchful care?
3:9.body: Rashi says the eyes are God's eyes, set on the Temple to make it greater, and Radak says they mean much protection from enemies. Malbim says Joshua carved a picture of seven eyes on the cornerstone.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעָה עֵינַיִם עַל שֵׁם עֵינֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says the seven eyes are named for the eyes of God, who means to make the House sevenfold greater.

sources.quote: שמירות רבות מאת האל
sources.says: Radak says the eyes mean much protection from God against the enemies.

sources.quote: שבעה עינים. ר״ל הרבה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says seven here just means many.

sources.quote: ויהושע חקק על האבן דמות של שבעה עינים
sources.says: Malbim says Joshua engraved an image of seven eyes on the stone.

3:9.headline: Untie the stone, or engrave it?
3:9.body: פתח can mean to open and also to engrave. Rashi reads it as untying the stone, undoing the enemies' plan that stopped the building, while Metzudat Zion reads it as carving designs into it.

sources.quote: מַתִּיר קִשּׁוּרֶיהָ, מֵפִיר עֲצַת הָאוֹיְבִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means untying its bonds, breaking the enemies' plan.

sources.quote: מפתח פתוחה. ענין חקיקת הציור
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means engraving a design.

sources.quote: כאלו היתה האבן קשורה כל הימים שבטלו המלאכה ועתה יפתח אותה
sources.says: Radak gives both: the stone was as if tied up while work stopped, or it means engraving.

9:1.headline: Hadrach: a town near Damascus, or 'sharp and soft'?
9:1.body: A sage in the midrash split חדרך into חד, sharp, and רך, soft: the Messiah, hard on the nations and gentle with Israel. A sage from Damascus objected that Hadrach is simply a place near his city.

sources.quote: זֶה מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא חַד לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת וְרַךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Yehudah, who reads the name as the Messiah, sharp toward idol worshippers and soft toward Israel.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֲנִי מִדַּמֶּשֶׂק, וְיֵשׁ מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ חַדְרָךְ
sources.says: Rashi cites Rabbi Yose, who says he is from Damascus and there is a place there named Hadrach.

sources.quote: חדרך. הוא מקום אצל דמשק
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says Hadrach is a place near Damascus.

sources.quote: חדרך - שם מלכות אדם או שם מלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Hadrach is the name of a kingdom or of a king.

9:1.headline: Damascus as God's resting place: Jerusalem will reach that far
9:1.body: מנוחה, rest, is a name for Jerusalem, as in 'this is my resting place forever'. So the midrash in Rashi reads the verse to say Jerusalem will one day stretch all the way to Damascus.

sources.quote: שֶׁעֲתִידָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם לִהְיוֹת מַגַּעַת עַד דַּמֶּשֶׂק, וְאֵין מְנוּחָתוֹ אֶלָּא יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
sources.says: Rashi's midrash says Jerusalem will one day reach Damascus, since 'his resting place' can only mean Jerusalem.

sources.quote: וגם דמשק תהיה מנוחתו ור״ל שכינת כבודו
sources.says: The Metzudat David says Damascus too will be his resting place, meaning the place of his presence.

9:4.headline: Make Tyre poor, or drive its people out?
9:4.body: The verb ירש can mean to make poor or to drive out. Rashi and Malbim read it as poverty: God will strip rich Tyre of its wealth. Radak and the Metzudat Zion read it as driving the city's people out.

sources.quote: יוֹרִישֶׁנָּה. לְשׁוֹן ״מוֹרִישׁ וּמַעֲשִׁיר״
sources.says: Rashi says it is the word in 'the Lord makes poor and makes rich'.

sources.quote: הנה ה' יורישנה שתורש מעשרה
sources.says: Malbim says Tyre will be stripped of its wealth.

sources.quote: הנה ה' יורישנה. ענין גרוש ושלוח
sources.says: Radak says the word means driving out and sending away.

sources.quote: יורישנה. ענין שלוח וגרושין
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means sending away and driving out.

9:4.headline: Her wealth, or her army, sunk in the sea?
9:4.body: חיל can mean wealth or an army. Rashi, Radak and the Aramaic translation say the sea will swallow Tyre's riches. The Metzudat David says God will drown her troops.

sources.quote: וְהִבְלִיעַ בְּתוֹךְ יַמִּים מָמוֹנָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says God will sink her money in the seas.

sources.quote: כל העושר והממון שבה שהיתה בוטחת בו יבא הים וישטף אותו
sources.says: Radak says the sea will wash away all the wealth she trusted in.

sources.quote: וְיִרְמֵי בְיַמָא עָתְרָהּ
sources.says: The Aramaic translation says he will cast her wealth into the sea.

sources.quote: וחיל צבאות עמה יכה בים ר״ל יטביעם במי הים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says he will strike her army in the sea, meaning drown them.

9:7.headline: A chief in Judah, or a place of teaching?
9:7.body: אלוף usually means a chief, and Ibn Ezra and Radak read it so: the Philistines who join Israel will be like Judah's leaders. Rashi and the Metzudat Zion read it from the verb 'to teach': the enemy's theaters will become places where Judah's princes teach Torah.

sources.quote: הנה הם כאלוף וכגדול שביהודה
sources.says: Radak says they will be like a chief, like the great ones of Judah.

sources.quote: כאלוף ביהודה - כמובחר שביהודה לעבודת השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means like the choicest in Judah in serving God.

sources.quote: וְהָיָה כְּאַלּוּף. לְשׁוֹן אִלּוּף וְלִמּוּד
sources.says: Rashi says the word comes from teaching and learning.

sources.quote: שֶׁעֲתִידִים שָׂרֵי יְהוּדָה לְלַמֵּד בָּהֶם תּוֹרָה בָּרַבִּים
sources.says: Rashi says their theaters and circuses are where Judah's princes will one day teach Torah in public.

sources.quote: כאלוף. ענין למוד כמו פן תאלף ארחותיו
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means learning, as in Proverbs' 'lest you learn his ways'.

9:7.headline: Ekron like the Jebusite: like Jerusalem, or paying tribute?
9:7.body: Jebus was Jerusalem's old name. The Metzudat David says Ekron's people will become pure-minded like Jerusalem's, while Radak and Ibn Ezra say Ekron will live among Israel and pay tribute, as the Jebusites did.

sources.quote: כִּיבוּסִי. יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says 'the Jebusite' means Jerusalem.

sources.quote: עקרון תשוב להיות כמו יבוס היא ירושלים ר״ל אנשיה יהיו נקיי הדעת כאנשי ירושלים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says Ekron will become like Jebus, which is Jerusalem: its people will be pure-minded like Jerusalem's.

sources.quote: תהיה עקרון כמו היבוסי יושב ירושלים שהיה יושב בתוך בני ישראל והיה למס עובד להן
sources.says: Radak says Ekron will be like the Jebusite who lived among Israel in Jerusalem and paid them tribute.

sources.quote: תתן מס כיבוסי שהיה בירושלם בימי דוד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Ekron will pay tribute like the Jebusite in Jerusalem in David's time.

9:9.headline: A humble king, or a poor one?
9:9.body: עני usually means poor. Rashi, Radak, the Metzudat Zion and the Aramaic translation read it as humble. Ibn Ezra reads it as truly poor: a king who at first had neither wealth nor horses.

sources.quote: עָנִי. עֲנְוְתָן
sources.says: Rashi says עני means humble.

sources.quote: עני. כמו ענין וכן ת"י ענותן
sources.says: Radak says it means humble, and the Aramaic translation renders it so.

sources.quote: עני. ר״ל מוכנע ועניו
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says it means lowly and humble.

sources.quote: הוּא עִנְוְתָן וְרָכֵיב עַל חֲמָרָא
sources.says: The Aramaic translation says 'he is humble and rides on a donkey'.

sources.quote: ובתחלתו לא היה לו לא עושר ולא סוסים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the king at first had neither wealth nor horses.

9:9.headline: A king on a donkey, not a war horse
9:9.body: Rashi says riding a donkey shows humility. Radak adds that it is not from need, since the whole world will be his: it shows Israel will no longer need horses and chariots, as the next verse says.

sources.quote: וְרוֹכֵב עַל חֲמוֹר. מִדַּת עֲנָוָה הִיא
sources.says: Rashi says riding on a donkey is a sign of humility.

sources.quote: לא מחסרון שהרי כל העולם יהיה ברשותו אלא מענוה ירכב על חמור ועוד להורות כי לא יצטרכו ישראל לסוסים ולרכב
sources.says: Radak says he rides a donkey not from need but from humility, and to show Israel will not need horses and chariots.

sources.quote: ורוכב על החמור הפך רוכב על סוס מוכן ליום מלחמה
sources.says: Malbim says riding a donkey is the opposite of riding a horse ready for war.

9:11.headline: Which covenant blood: Sinai, or circumcision?
9:11.body: Rashi says 'the blood of your covenant' is the blood sprinkled on the people at Sinai. Radak and the Metzudat David say it is the blood of circumcision, which Israel kept in exile more than any other command.

sources.quote: בִּזְכוּת דַּם הַבְּרִית שֶׁנִּזְרַק עֲלֵיכֶם בְּסִינַי
sources.says: Rashi says it is for the merit of the covenant blood sprinkled on you at Sinai.

sources.quote: והוא דם המילה שהחזיקו בו ישראל בגלות יותר מכל המצות
sources.says: Radak says it is the blood of circumcision, which Israel held on to in exile more than any other command.

sources.quote: בעבור זכות דם בריתך היא מצות מילה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the covenant blood is the command of circumcision.

sources.quote: בעבור דם הברית אשר כרת השם עם יוצאי מצרים. ויש אומרים: בעבור מצות המילה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra gives both: the covenant God made with those who left Egypt, or the command of circumcision.

9:11.headline: A pit with no water: what the missing water means
9:11.body: The exile is pictured as a dry pit. The Metzudat David says a dry pit is where snakes and scorpions live, like the nations that harmed Israel. Radak's father says the missing water stands for prophecy, which stopped in exile.

sources.quote: והמשיל הגלות בבל לבור שאין בו מים לפי שבבור כזה מצויים נחשים ועקרבי׳ המזיקים
sources.says: The Metzudat David says the exile is compared to a waterless pit because such a pit has harmful snakes and scorpions.

sources.quote: פירש מים נבואה בדרך משל שנסתמה הנבואה בגלות
sources.says: Radak says his father read the water as a figure for prophecy, which was shut off in exile.

9:12.headline: Return to the stronghold: Jerusalem, your strength, or God?
9:12.body: בצרון comes from the word for a fortress. The Metzudat David says the stronghold is Jerusalem, Rashi says it means your strength and honor, and Radak's father says the stronghold is God.

sources.quote: לבצרון. מל׳ מבצר
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word comes from מבצר, fortress.

sources.quote: שובו לירושלים עיר מבצרכם
sources.says: The Metzudat David says it means return to Jerusalem, your fortress city.

sources.quote: שׁוּבוּ לְבִצָּרוֹן. לְכֹחֲכֶם וְלִכְבוֹדְכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it means return to your strength and your honor.

sources.quote: ופי' שובו לבצרון שובו לאל יתברך שהוא מבצר ומגדל עוז
sources.says: Radak says his father read it as 'return to God', who is a fortress and a strong tower.

9:12.headline: 'Prisoners of hope': held in exile, or tied to hope?
9:12.body: Radak reads it plainly: people held in exile who hope to be freed. The Metzudat David reads it as a figure: they are bound to their hope as if tied to it, and it never leaves them.

sources.quote: בעבור שהיו בגלות והיו אסורים ומקוים לגאולה
sources.says: Radak says they were in exile, held as prisoners and hoping for redemption.

sources.quote: המקווים לה׳ בכל זמן כאלו קשורים בתקוה ולא תתפרד מהם והוא ענין מליצה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says those who always hope in God are as if tied to hope, which never parts from them; it is a figure of speech.

9:13.headline: 'I filled Ephraim': drawing a bow with full strength
9:13.body: To 'fill' a bow is to grip it and pull it hard, as when Jehu 'filled his hand with the bow'. Rashi says the verse leaves a word out: God filled Ephraim's hand with a bow.

sources.quote: מִקְרָא קָצָר הוּא, כְּמוֹ קֶשֶׁת מִלֵּאתִי יַד אֶפְרָיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the verse is shortened and means 'I filled Ephraim's hand with a bow'.

sources.quote: מלאתי. זה הלשון יאמר על אחיזת הקשת בכח
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says this phrase is used for gripping a bow with force.

sources.quote: והוא מתיחת הקשת בכל כחו לירות החץ
sources.says: Radak says it means drawing the bow with all one's strength to shoot the arrow.

9:14.headline: Storms of Teman: a south wind, or an attack on Teman?
9:14.body: תימן can mean the south or the land of Teman. Ibn Ezra and Radak say God comes in storm winds from the south. Rashi and the Metzudat David say he storms against Teman, which for Rashi is Antiochus's army.

sources.quote: בסערות תימן - רוח דרומית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a south wind.

sources.quote: וזכר תימן שהיא פאת דרום כי משם תבא רוח סערה
sources.says: Radak says Teman is the south side, where storm winds come from.

sources.quote: לְסַעֵר אֶת אַנְשֵׁי תֵימָן, הֵם חֵיל אַנְטִיוֹכוּס
sources.says: Rashi says God will storm against the men of Teman, who are Antiochus's army.

sources.quote: ילך ברוח סערה בשטף אף אל תימן להחריבה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says he will go in a storm wind to Teman to destroy it.

9:15.headline: Two kinds of stones: sling stones and crown jewels
9:15.body: The enemy are called אבני קלע, sling stones, and the next verse calls Judah אבני נזר, crown jewels. Radak and the Metzudat David say the contrast is chosen: stones made to be thrown against stones set in a crown.

sources.quote: וכנה בני יון אבני קלע שהם אבני חצות שקולעים בהם הקלעים לפי שכנה בני יהודה בהפכה אבני נזר
sources.says: Radak says the Greeks are called sling stones because, in contrast, Judah is called crown jewels.

sources.quote: המשיל שרים לאבנים שמקלעים אותם הנבזים העומדים לזריקה
sources.says: The Metzudat David says, since Judah's leaders are compared to crown jewels, the enemy's officers are compared to worthless stones made for throwing.

sources.quote: הֵם הַיְּוָנִים שֶׁהֵם מְלֻמְּדֵי קֶשֶׁת וְלִקְלֹעַ בָּאֶבֶן
sources.says: Rashi says the sling stones are the Greeks, who were trained with the bow and the sling.

9:16.headline: Raised like a banner, or shining with miracles?
9:16.body: נס means a banner raised on a pole, and also a miracle. Radak and the Metzudat Zion read מתנוססות as 'raised high', like a banner. Rashi reads it as the Hasmonean priests lifted up by miracles.

sources.quote: מתנוססות. מל׳ נס והוא ענין הרמה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word comes from נס, banner, and means raising up.

sources.quote: וכן נס ענין גבהות ורוממות כי נושא הנס מגביה ומרומם אותו על ראש העם
sources.says: Radak says נס means height, since the banner carrier lifts it above the people.

sources.quote: יִהְיוּ מִתְנוֹסְסִים בְּנִסִּים עַל אַדְמָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says the Hasmonean priests will be lifted up with miracles on their land.

9:17.headline: Wine that sets young women singing, or grapes from untouched soil?
9:17.body: Rashi and the Metzudat Zion read ינובב from ניב, speech: the wine will set young women singing. Rashi also brings a reading from 'to grow': wine grown in untouched, 'virgin' soil.

sources.quote: ינובב. ענין דבור כמו ינוב חכמה
sources.says: The Metzudat Zion says the word means speech, as in 'utters wisdom'.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר יְנוֹבֵב בְּתוּלוֹת בְּנִיב שִׁיר וְשִׂמְחָה
sources.says: Rashi says the wine will move the young women to words of song and joy.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ פּוֹתְרִין אֲשֶׁר יְנוֹבֵב וְיִצְמַח בְּקַרְקַע בְּתוּלָה
sources.says: Rashi says some read it as wine that grows in virgin soil.

sources.quote: מגזרת: ינובון בשיבה. והנכון: מגזרת ניב שפתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra mentions a reading from 'they will flourish', but says the right one is from 'speech of the lips'.
